title: Dynamics GP to Business Central – What does my migrated GP Historical Data look like in Business Central
summary: After a Dynamics GP to Business Central migration, historical transactions are stored in special tables rather than as ledger entries. Sales and receivables history, including applied payments, is shown through factbox tiles on the Customer List, and vendor history works the same way. Financial journal history is reached from the Chart of Accounts through the GP Detail Snapshot action.
key_points: Historical transactions migrate into special tables rather than creating new ledger entries, since they represent already-paid transactions
Sales and receivables transactions are accessible via factbox tiles on the Customer List page, showing both order details and applied payments
Financial historical data can be viewed through the Chart of Accounts page using the GP Detail Snapshot option, allowing drill-down by transaction or by account
Users can access historical purchasing data the same way as sales data by selecting the Vendor List instead of the Sales List
Historical data can be retained in a separate reference company even if not using the migrated company for live transactions

quotes.text: The migration of the Historical transactions is one of the first questions you I'm asked on almost every Business Central project.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights that historical data migration is a critical concern for organizations moving to Business Central, and the GP migration tools address this effectively.

quotes.text: Having historical GP data available inside Business Central helps make the new system a true single point of reference.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the strategic value of complete historical data visibility for making Business Central the primary system for all business information.
